BiblicalUsage: Ba'ath means to be terrified, to be struck with sudden fear. The evil spirit terrified Saul and his servants said, behold, an evil spirit from God troubleth thee; Daniel fell on his face in fear when Gabriel came near; the waters of the sea terrified the prophet; and Job says the terrors of God set themselves in array against him. Fear that comes like a wave and overwhelms.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that there is a fear that comes from God and a fear that comes from the enemy, and Daniel shows me the difference: he fell on his face before Gabriel, and the angel lifted him up. The fear of the Lord does not crush; it raises.
